chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When you pray (Salaat) upon the believer, supplicate for him and strive for him in supplication; and if he was standing (in prayer) but of weak understanding, then exclaim Takbeer and say: 'O Allah, forgive those who repented and followed Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blaze.'

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer over the deceased (funeral prayer/salat al-janazah context)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفُ: The weak one (one who is standing but lacks full knowledge/understanding)
key_terms.الْوَاقِفُ: The one standing (referring to a state of being in prayer but not fully knowledgeable)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for a deceased believer who had limited knowledge or understanding?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to define the spiritual etiquette of 'Salaat' (prayer/du'a) over the deceased, emphasizing that the quality of supplication should be intensified for those who were 'waqif'—standing in faith but lacking deep gnosis or full recognition of Wilayah. By quoting Quran 40:7, the Imam links the intercessory prayer directly to the divine promise of forgiveness for those who turn to God, highlighting the Shia theological nuance that incomplete knowledge does not preclude salvation if accompanied by sincere adherence to the path. This hadith serves as a practical guide for mourners to elevate the spiritual status of the deceased through targeted, earnest du'a.
